Clonezilla is probably your best bet for full drive/partition backup. There are some caveats like making sure the master boot record is backed up/restored and you'll want to boot a live USB/CD of clonezilla/ubcd as cloning partitions that are in use can be problematic.

As for your backup drive, the only time you might have problems is if the backup drive is smaller. Be sure to use the device->image option with compression and you will have a smaller backup image file to easily restore by just reversing the process. As with most Linux stuff it takes a little trial and error to get it just right, but once you have it down, you're set.

Thanks, I'll try clonezilla again, maybe just use the advanced options and go until it actually decides to work... Edit: I just want to be able to reimage my machine if I screw up the current version. I keep all pictures/docs/files on a separate drive so I am only concerned with the installed programs and the OS itself.

The best way is to use snapshots; btrfs or LVM are both good, but they do require you to set them up prior to installation, really. Maybe consider them next time you install a distro. I take btrfs snapshots of my SSD every day and before every update, and if anything breaks I can just roll back. Also, snapshots don't use up much space, since they only store the difference between the live system and the snapshot itself (in btrfs at least.)

Without using snapshots, as others have said, your best bet is Clonezilla.
